author: m. b. nelson
title: San José announces FIFA World Cup festivities and events for June and July
text:
The City of San José announced on June 3 that it will host a series of events, watch parties, and concerts in celebration of the FIFA 2026 World Cup from June 11 to July 11. All teams playing in Bay Area World Cup matches will stay and practice in San José, with Team Paraguay based in the city throughout the tournament.
City Manager Jennifer Maguire said, “San José is thrilled to welcome visitors, athletes, and fans from across the globe to fly, stay, and play in our City and experience our community, our culture, and the energy that makes our City a world-class center for sports entertainment.”
In partnership with the San Jose Earthquakes soccer club, San Pedro Square will serve as an entertainment zone featuring one of the largest fan fest celebrations globally. The area will host watch parties for all 104 FIFA matches along with family activities. Festivities begin on June 11 at San Pedro Square Market with watch parties for Mexico vs. South Africa at noon and Korea Republic vs. Czechia at 7 p.m., while Eastridge Mall hosts its first neighborhood watch party during Mexico’s match.
Additional events include a Zeds Dead concert at Discovery Meadow on June 20, a drone show at Lake Cunningham on July 4, as well as soccer-themed art exhibits. Mayor Matt Mahan said, “We’re just a week away from the world seeing everything San José has to offer. The celebration starts at San Pedro Square with the Earthquakes takeover and one of the biggest watch parties in the country — and extends across our city as we welcome fans from around the globe to experience San José.”
Earthquakes President Jared Shawlee said their organization is prepared to help make these among “the biggest FIFA World Cup watch parties in the region.” John Poch of the San Jose Sports Authority highlighted past World Cups hosted by South Bay: “The South Bay has a proud World Cup legacy… We are honored to welcome the world back for a third FIFA World Cup.” He added that their goal is “to unite our community” through these celebrations.
Soccer celebrations are funded through corporate sponsorships raised by SJ26 program partners including local government agencies and organizations such as SJ26 initiative collaborators. Fans can access schedules or participate via Game On App or visit sj26.sanjose.org/world-cup for event details.
The City of San Jose promotes cultural diversity through initiatives like Japanese Friendship Garden and Mexican Heritage Plaza; maintains historical sites such as Kelley Park’s museum; features unique replicas like Statehouse buildings; serves neighborhoods throughout Santa Clara Valley; operates under an elected mayor-council system; aims to deliver quality public services—all according to the city’s historical context page, official mission page, and official charter page.
